headline: Standard Chartered's chief executive, Bill Winters, said AI needs stronger regulation and international cooperation, and that jobs needing human judgment will remain.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a bank chief's clear call for AI rules plus job figures, but they are his own claims.
importance_line: Bank staff and customers are affected first, and regulators hear a call for rules from an industry insider, but the job figures are the bank's own and no policy follows.
summary: CNA reports that Winters, in an interview on 9 Oct at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore, said "very few industries" have needed regulation more than AI, noting that a new aspirin formulation takes three years to clear regulators while AI has no guardrails, and warned that "some bad things will happen". He said the bank has automated almost 25 per cent of its earlier roles yet its headcount has grown and about 85 per cent of displaced staff were retrained, with roles needing human judgment, such as wealth-management relationship managers, staying in demand; these are the bank's own figures.
